topics: What does it mean to design a system?

chapters.title: A system is a promise
topics: What does it mean to design a system?
HLD vs LLD vs software architecture.

illustrations.title: The boundary follows the promise
illustrations.caption: A user asks the application to remember a task. The store is inside the service responsibility boundary even if a different team operates it.
illustrations.why: It separates the user-visible obligation from the process that happens to run the code.

illustrations.title: Data becomes state through a transition
illustrations.caption: Given an empty collection and the create command, the state gains task 7 and the caller receives its identifier. Repeating that command is a separate design question.
illustrations.why: A concrete transition exposes both the state owner and the effect that a retry could duplicate.

illustrations.title: HLD and LLD ask connected questions
illustrations.caption: The high-level view places persistent state and communication boundaries. The low-level view explains how application components enforce behavior inside a process.
illustrations.why: Both views must agree about who commits state and who reports success.

illustrations.title: From a working demo to a recoverable write
illustrations.caption: The naive program works within one run. A restart disproves its persistence promise. Committing before success fixes that failure under the storage assumptions; it does not by itself solve lost replies.
illustrations.why: The improvement is tied to a reproducible failure rather than an arbitrary desire for more components.

chapters.title: Boundaries that make change local
topics: Coupling, cohesion, modularity, separation of concerns.

illustrations.title: An innocent feature crosses every responsibility
illustrations.caption: In the tangled implementation, formatting, business rules, and persistence all know the mutable representation. Changing a field or invariant can break several paths.
illustrations.why: Dependency arrows identify the concrete knowledge that makes a change spread.

illustrations.title: Separate responsibilities inside one process
illustrations.caption: The adapter translates input, the service owns task rules, and the repository owns persistence operations. All three can be ordinary functions in one deployment.
illustrations.why: A module boundary can reduce change propagation without adding a network boundary.

illustrations.title: Dependency direction differs from execution direction
illustrations.caption: Dashed arrows mean source-level dependencies. At runtime the task service calls the concrete adapter through the agreed contract; there is no extra repository server.
illustrations.why: It prevents the common mistake of interpreting every diagram arrow as a network request.

illustrations.title: Abstraction narrows the question at each layer
illustrations.caption: Each layer hides details but relies on a narrower promise below it. A successful application call cannot offer stronger persistence than its storage and operating assumptions support.
illustrations.why: Abstraction reduces what a caller must know; it cannot remove physical dependencies.

chapters.title: Requirements become decisions
topics: Why the simplest sufficient design is often preferable.

illustrations.title: Make a vague quality measurable
illustrations.caption: The quality scenario names a stimulus, an environment, and a response. This example concerns process restart; it makes no claim about losing the only disk or an entire region.
illustrations.why: A precise scope makes a design falsifiable and reveals the assumptions still needing discussion.

illustrations.title: A decision is a testable hypothesis
illustrations.caption: An ADR records why a choice fits current evidence and when to revisit it. The feedback dependency returns changed evidence to requirements analysis.
illustrations.why: It keeps a previously sensible choice from becoming an unquestioned permanent rule.

illustrations.title: A hard constraint comes before a preference score
illustrations.caption: An in-memory design is infeasible for the chosen restart promise, however cheap or quick it is. Weighted scores compare only candidates that pass the hard constraints.
illustrations.why: It distinguishes a preference trade-off from violating an invariant.

illustrations.title: Healthy traffic does not prove durable data
illustrations.caption: Availability and durability require different observations. A fully reachable service can lose data; a temporarily unreachable store can retain all committed data.
illustrations.why: Separate evidence prevents an uptime dashboard from being treated as proof of data safety.

chapters.title: One application, many architectural views
topics: Architecture diagrams: C4 model, context, container, component, deployment, sequence.

illustrations.title: C4 changes the level of detail
illustrations.caption: The dashed arrows mean a change in abstraction, not a runtime call. C4 containers are applications or data stores; they are not synonymous with operating-system containers.
illustrations.why: Choose the view that answers a real reader question, rather than drawing all four levels automatically.

illustrations.title: A deployment view locates the single points of failure
illustrations.caption: The example has one machine with a local store. Module separation has not created redundancy; host or disk loss can still remove the whole service.
illustrations.why: Deployment placement exposes correlated failure that logical component boxes can hide.

illustrations.title: A lost response makes the outcome uncertain
illustrations.caption: Commit precedes the lost response. A timeout cannot distinguish this case from a failure before commit. Retrying a create without a deduplication contract can create another task.
illustrations.why: A sequence explains the ambiguity that a static architecture diagram leaves out.

illustrations.title: Architecture evolves when an assumption fails
illustrations.caption: Persistence addresses restart. An API addresses shared remote access. Redundancy and data distribution require their own failure, correctness, and load analysis; they are not a free final step.
illustrations.why: The sequence is a set of justified changes, not a universal maturity ladder.
